title: Request authentication context cleanup
objective: Create one request Authentication object at the Endpoint middleware boundary so controllers only authorize credential type and services directly request user, organization, or project context.
acceptance_criteria: Endpoint middleware stores exactly one *types.Authentication in CTX_.
Authentication contains AuthType, optional actor identity, and available user, organization, and project contexts.
Authentication.Actor() returns the actor or an explicit unavailable error; organization and service authentication remain valid without a durable actor in Phase 1D.
Authorize returns *Authentication and Scope returns the same object when its AuthType is allowed.
Authentication.UserContext(), OrganizationContext(), and ProjectContext() return explicit values or errors.
Credential-specific principles do not gain fake context methods.
Endpoint controllers use only Authorize and Scope for authentication policy.
Endpoint services accept *Authentication and contain no optionalUserID, requireMutationContext, RequireUser, RequireOrganization, RequireProject, concrete type assertions, or AuthType switches.
Persistent Endpoint mutations continue to require UserContext and ProjectContext until actor dual-write is approved; services enforce both directly without helper utilities.
Endpoint invocation logs retain the existing optional legacy user attribution behavior and leave legacy user fields zero when UserContext is unavailable.
Organization scope may Invoke public endpoints; private endpoint access requires ProjectContext.
Fork, Probe, and Update return Unimplemented after authentication and Scope until a resource-owning implementation exists.
No identifier, type, function, or comment introduced by this phase uses normalize or normalized naming.
out_of_scope: Migrating non-Endpoint binaries from legacy authentication accessors
Deleting compatibility Require functions while non-Endpoint callers remain
Audit actor dual-write or legacy column removal

principles.KISS: One concrete request object with direct context methods.
principles.YAGNI: No registries, generic context helpers, reflection, or credential-type switches outside middleware construction.
principles.ownership: Middleware owns authentication construction; controllers own allowed types; services own resource context requirements.
principles.explicit_contracts: Unavailable context is an error and never inferred from zero values.
principles.fail_safe: Private and project operations fail without ProjectContext.
principles.least_privilege: Scope approval never grants resource access.
principles.reversibility: Revert Phase 1D independently of Phase 1C middleware and schema changes.

required_tests: Authentication context accessor and Scope tests
Boundary tests for all four credential classes and context construction
Controller source contract test prohibiting Require calls
Endpoint service tests for user, project, service, and organization behavior
Legacy audit fields remain zero for actors without UserContext
risks: Endpoint service interface signatures change from SimplePrinciple to *Authentication.
Legacy audit columns cannot represent non-user actors; persistent Endpoint mutations therefore remain user-required until actor dual-write.
Missing context construction at middleware could deny valid requests; boundary tests cover every credential class.
rollback: Revert the Phase 1D commit; Phase 1C middleware, actor schema, and historical confirmations remain unchanged.
